did: I built the first four steps of the APK walkthrough videos and landed them. The walk runner now walks the real phone app on an emulator as well as a web page, on one week of made-up Jobs data, with a stand-in microphone so a take is recorded and played back. The walkthrough is the promo with a chapter per stop; the owner approved its look, and its first render, captions only, is on the prototype page. I also took the owner's real contact details out of the Jobs sample, replacing them with a made-up person. Then I started the honest friction the narration will speak: the Jobs wing now says, in the existing vocabulary, which step of a pick, the record or the interview week is on screen and for how long, and every module now says whether its opening is measured at all, so a module that sends nothing reads not measured rather than silent.

calls.title: C860: how to build the APK walkthrough (WALK's reach)
options: Generalize the existing walk runner over stages, with a story sample as a stand-in home routes file and Playwright's Android driver doing the walking
Use Maestro's YAML flows on the emulator
Use Appium with a WebDriver client
Record the emulator's screen and cut it by hand
calls.why: Everything the walkthrough needs already existed in part: the web walk runner and its walk file, the stand-in home, and the Android driver Snips Capture uses on real work. Extending them at their family's level adds one stage, not a second runner, and keeps the output the promo already reads.
calls.undo: Put the walk runner's steps back to the old tap-and-hold shape with the sandbox inlined, and drop the APK stage, apps/mobile/walk and the Jobs story sample.

left: WALK5 step 2: home aggregates the friction measures the owner allowed in C861 (days opened out of 28 per module; finished vs left part-way and median time per step; Applying's debrief friction), under the fewer-than-5 rule, from the events #3344 now sends. Not started: it is home's work and needed #3344 first.
WALK5 step 3: each walkthrough stop gets spoken words for Kokoro, each screen retimed to its caption's speech, and a friction burn-in per stop. Waits on step 2's aggregate.
WALK5 step 4: the Jobs walkthrough rendered on home, proven twice-equal, shown in Studio's Renders. Waits on steps 2 and 3.
Taps per step are not measured: that needs a new field on the engagement event, which is the owner's call, so I did not add it.
Whether a module was opened is known per module, not per surface, so Jobs on the desktop is counted only by its own take. Left for a later story.
WALK2's Rust Rounds week and sending the take home as a walk stop are not built; both are on #3282.
The APK walk uses the debug build's whole-screen pictures and does not freeze the page clock, so in-app times can drift by minutes. Known gaps, noted in #3341.
